# primitives.library: DropLast

```plato

    // Every element except the last n — the complement of Take, and the
    // back-end twin of Skip. Precondition: 0 <= n <= Count.
    //
    // Take/Skip/TakeLast/DropLast are a complete 2x2: Take and TakeLast KEEP n
    // from the front and the back, Skip and DropLast REMOVE n from the front and
    // the back. This was `Drop` until plato-378, which both duplicated `Skip`
    // and left the remove-from-the-back cell empty. The name now agrees with
    // `Collections.DropLast(ISliceable)`, which is defined identically
    // as `Slice(0, Count - count)`, and with the C# runtime's
    // `Ara3D.Collections.LinqArray.DropLast`.
    DropLast(xs: Array<$T>, n: Integer): Array<$T>
        => xs.Take(xs.Count - n);

    // The last n elements. Precondition: 0 <= n <= Count.
    TakeLast(xs: Array<$T>, n: Integer): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(n, i => xs[xs.Count - n + i]);

    // `count` elements starting at `from` — the COUNT-based sub-range, and the
    // only one. Everything named Slice takes endpoints.
    // Precondition: the window is in range.
    SubArray(xs: Array<$T>, from: Integer, count: Integer): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(count, i => xs[from + i]);

    // The half-open window [from, exclusiveTo), holding exclusiveTo - from
    // elements. Matches `ISliceable.Slice` exactly, so `Slice` means the same
    // thing on every receiver in the tree (plato-378).
    // Precondition: 0 <= from <= exclusiveTo <= Count.
    Slice(xs: Array<$T>, from: Integer, exclusiveTo: Integer): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(exclusiveTo - from, i => xs[from + i]);

    // Every nth element starting at index 0. The count rounds UP: a 5-element
    // array stepped by 2 yields indices 0, 2 and 4. Precondition: n > 0.
    EveryNth(self: Array<$T>, n: Integer): Array<$T>
        => MapRange((self.Count + n - 1) / n, i => self[i * n]);

    // The element at n reduced modulo Count, so an index may run off the END and
    // wrap. The idiom behind closed-polygon edge walks: points.AtModulo(i+1).
    // Preconditions: the array is not empty, and n is not negative — a negative
    // n leaves the remainder negative rather than wrapping to the tail.
    AtModulo(xs: Array<$T>, n: Integer): $T
        => xs[n % xs.Count];

    //==
    // # Array — construction

    // n copies of x. The count comes first because the compiler requires a
    // concrete first parameter, so the V1 form Repeat(x, n) became Repeat(n, x).
    Repeat(n: Integer, x: $T): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(n, i => x);

    // The array with value appended after the last element.
    Append(self: Array<$T>, value: $T): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(self.Count + 1, i => i < self.Count ? self[i] : value);

    // The array with value inserted before the first element.
    Prepend(self: Array<$T>, value: $T): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(self.Count + 1, i => i == 0 ? value : self[i - 1]);

    // The two arrays joined end to end.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concatenation)
    Concatenate(xs: Array<$T>, ys: Array<$T>): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(xs.Count + ys.Count, i => i < xs.Count ? xs[i] : ys[i - xs.Count]);

    //==
    // # Array — predicates
    //
    // Folds rather than loops with an early exit, which a Plato body cannot
    // write: All and Any visit every element. Boolean && and || short-circuit
    // (docs/SEMANTICS.md section 6), so once the answer is decided the
    // predicate is not called again; a backend that wants the loop itself to
    // stop early supplies it through the override table.

    // True when every element satisfies the predicate (vacuously true when empty).
    All(xs: Array<$T>, f: Function1<$T, Boolean>): Boolean
        => xs.Reduce(true, (acc, x) => acc && f(x));

    // True when at least one element satisfies the predicate (false when empty).
    Any(xs: Array<$T>, f: Function1<$T, Boolean>): Boolean
        => xs.Reduce(false, (acc, x) => acc || f(x));

    //==
    // # Array2D
    //
    // The IIndexable2D obligations the two extent FIELDS do not already cover,
    // plus construction. Row-major, matching Collections.FlattenIndex.

    // The total cell count: every element of the backing store.
    Count(self: Array2D<$T>): Integer
        => self.Elements.Count;

    // The cell at a row-major flat index. Precondition: 0 <= n < Count.
    At(self: Array2D<$T>, n: Integer): $T
        => self.Elements[n];

    // The cell at (column, row). Precondition: the cell is in range.
    At(self: Array2D<$T>, column: Integer, row: Integer): $T
        => self.Elements[row * self.ColumnCount + column];

    // A columns x rows grid whose cell (c, r) is f(c, r).
    MakeArray2D(columns: Integer, rows: Integer, f: Function2<Integer, Integer, $T>): Array2D<$T>
    {
        var elements = MapRange(columns * rows, i => f(i % columns, i / columns));
        return (elements, columns, rows);
    }

    // The cells of one column, top to bottom. Precondition: col is in range.
    Column(self: Array2D<$T>, col: Integer): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(self.RowCount, r => self.At(col, r));

    // The cells of one row, left to right. Precondition: row is in range.
    Row(self: Array2D<$T>, row: Integer): Array<$T>
        => MapRange(self.ColumnCount, c => self.At(c, row));

    // A grid of the same shape holding f applied to every cell.
    Map(xs: Array2D<$T1>, f: Function1<$T1, $T2>): Array2D<$T2>
    {
        var elements = xs.Elements.Map(f);
        return (elements, xs.ColumnCount, xs.RowCount);
    }

    // The array cut into rows of `size`, as a grid. A trailing partial row is
    // dropped. Precondition: size > 0.
    Slices(xs: Array<$T>, size: Integer): Array2D<$T>
    {
        var rows = xs.Count / size;
        return (xs.Take(rows * size), size, rows);
    }

    // The grid whose cell (c, r) is func(columns[c], rows[r]).
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartesian_product)
    CartesianProduct(columns: Array<$TColumn>, rows: Array<$TRow>, func: Function2<$TColumn, $TRow, $TResult>): Array2D<$TResult>
        => MakeArray2D(columns.Count, rows.Count, (c, r) => func(columns[c], rows[r]));

    //==
    // # Array3D

    // The total cell count: every element of the backing store.
    Count(self: Array3D<$T>): Integer
        => self.Elements.Count;

    // The cell at a row-major flat index. Precondition: 0 <= n < Count.
    At(self: Array3D<$T>, n: Integer): $T
        => self.Elements[n];

    // The cell at (column, row, layer). Precondition: the cell is in range.
    At(self: Array3D<$T>, column: Integer, row: Integer, layer: Integer): $T
        => self.Elements[(layer * self.RowCount + row) * self.ColumnCount + column];

    // A columns x rows x layers volume whose cell (c, r, l) is f(c, r, l).
    MakeArray3D(columns: Integer, rows: Integer, layers: Integer, f: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, $T>): Array3D<$T>
    {
        var plane = columns * rows;
        var elements = MapRange(plane * layers, i => f(i % columns, (i / columns) % rows, i / plane));
        return (elements, columns, rows, layers);
    }
```
